label: last two copy outputs (short sequences, or o/i/e/r/p input)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and almost entirely on the last two copy steps (to_go <= 1 holds 92% of activation mass). It is strongest in short sequences: L=3 and L=4 give 66% of the mass, and the largest activations are at the final step of L=3 sequences (e.g. q o e <DEL> q [o]). In longer sequences it fires near the end mostly when the current input token is o, i, e, r or p (o has the highest rate). It does not fire mid-copy far from the end, and rarely fires 3 or more steps before the end. The token dependence in long sequences is graded, not a clean set, so precision and recall are incomplete.
